Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 25-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Human Computer Interaction [NPT_4131]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Apply the principles of User-Centered Design (UCD) to an IoT-based home automation system.             (5)  
  Experiment with different interaction modalities (touch, voice, gesture) and explain how they can  
  A)           solve usability issues for elderly users.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Analyze the differences between Graphical User Interface (GUI) and Natural User Interface (NUI).       (3)  
  Compare their usability in real-world contexts and provide a short conclusion about which is more  
  effective for accessibility.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)           Inspect how ethical considerations influence the IRB approval process and discover one possible        (2)  
  risk if these standards are not followed.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Utilize the concept of triangulation to describe how multiple data sources can be combined to          (5)  
  enhance the reliability of findings in HCI research.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Solve the issue of data misinterpretation by proposing three steps that ensure accurate statistical    (3)  
  analysis and reporting in quantitative research.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Identify two common pitfalls that researchers often face while applying for IRB approval and briefly   (2)  
  explain how these can impact the research timeline.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                Apply the concept of the Double Diamond design model to explain how prototyping fits within the     (5)  
  stages of divergent and convergent thinking. Illustrate your answer with an example of designing an  
  A)           accessible user interface for visually impaired users.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Given a Mid-Fi student-portal prototype, examine the design and inspect its core flows. Test for       (3)  
  three usability/accessibility risks specifically highlighted in the talk (e.g., navigation clarity,  
  
  Page #1

affordance indicators like dropdown arrows, font/contrast scalability).  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)               Demonstrate how two ethical challenges researchers may arise during data gathering can be                  (2)  
  minimized through IRB-approved protocols.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)                       Compare the role of Lo-Fi and Hi-Fi prototyping in refining a product's design. Contrast how each          (5)  
  stage contributes differently to user feedback and design iteration.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)               Apply three key factors to decide when to transition from low-fidelity to mid-fidelity prototypes in an    (3)  
  iterative design process.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)               Divide the IoT design challenges mentioned into technical and ethical categories, and discover one (2)  
  key user-centered solution for each.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)                       Apply your understanding of qualitative and quantitative data gathering methods to design an               (5)  
  experiment that measures user satisfaction with a newly developed interface. Explain how you  
  A)               would balance statistical validity with ethical considerations.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)               Categorize the different data gathering methods used in HCI research.                                      (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)               Utilize a conversational AI tool (such as Alexa or ChatGPT) to explain how HCI design principles           (2)  
  like accessibility and user engagement can improve user interaction quality.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
